summary: Deschutes NF tower built 1932 with an L-4 cab; volunteers dismantled it in July 2006 and the cab went to the High Desert Museum; no source confirms a rebuild or what remains on the butte.

facts.design: L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk atop a 30-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: Dismantled July 2006; cab bundled and stored at the High Desert Museum; the planned rebuild is not confirmed by any source read

staffing.status: abandoned for several years before 2006 (firelookout.com); last named lookout in the sources read is W.T. Curtis, 1948

events.note: Tower erected by August 1932 with an L-4 cab (Forest Lookouts newspaper excerpts; NHLR says built 1932). firelookout.com says built in 1933
Lee Smith named as fireman-lookout in August 1932; a July 1932 report had named Paddy Ryan as the planned lookout
Garage built (NHLR); a garage was under construction in October 1933 per Forest Lookouts
Charles Shaw, lookout, flashed a mirror to a plane during an aerial wild horse roundup
W.T. Curtis, lookout-fireman, split duties with the Tumalo Mountain lookout
Garage moved to Sparks Lake and converted into a cabin
Original pine tower legs replaced with tamarack (firelookout.com says larch)
Engineering firm inspected the tower; recommended removing the lower stairs; cab beams appeared rotten
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register
Volunteers dismantled the tower July 10 to 15, 2006; hardware salvaged for future restorations
Cab bundled and stored at the High Desert Museum south of Bend, pending a planned rebuild

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the tower was built in 1933. NHLR says 1932, and the August 1932 newspaper excerpts on the Forest Lookouts page show the tower erected that month. The story uses 1932 for the tower and 1933 for the garage.

A July 1932 Bend Bulletin item named Paddy Ryan as the planned lookout, a July 1932 Oregonian item named Pat Ryan, and by August 1932 Lee Smith is the lookout stationed there. The sources do not say why the plan changed.
NHLR says tamarack poles, firelookout.com says larch poles, and Forest Lookouts says tamarack timbers. Tamarack and larch are two common names for the same tree, so this is a wording difference.

notes_for_editor: Gone: dismantled July 2006 by volunteers; cab stored at the High Desert Museum; the rebuild is planned but unconfirmed. One WebSearch found no current status and only old pages. A 2026 Nugget article on the museum expansion was checked only in part (the first section) and is not cited. Elevation conflict: the brief's 1,230.5 m matches NHLR (4,037 ft); firelookout.com gives 5,697 ft, which is not used. The brief's access 'unknown' is kept out of facts because no source describes access. No new photos found. Reads: NHLR (2), firelookout.com (1), Forest Lookouts (2), firelookout.org list (1); one WebSearch.
